narrative: The psychiatrist voluntarily surrendered a Georgia medical license by a two-page Voluntary Surrender, acknowledging that the surrender has the same effect as revocation and waiving the right to a hearing. The document states no reason for the surrender and contains no allegations, findings or admissions; it notes only that if reinstatement were ever sought, the Board would have access to its investigative file in the matter and the physician would have to show the ability to practice with reasonable skill and safety.
cases.outcome: Voluntary surrender of license, with the effect of revocation; accepted by the Board effective February 5, 2021. Reinstatement only at the Board's discretion on a showing of fitness to practice.

narrative: The Board received an initial complaint alleging professional misconduct by the psychiatrist, investigated possible violations of the Medical Practice Act, and authorized service of Formal Charges. Without any findings being entered on the allegations, he signed an Agreement to Relinquish License to Practice Medicine, waiving a hearing, further proceedings and judicial review, and gave up "forevermore" his right to practice medicine in South Carolina. He agreed that he will not be eligible to reapply for a South Carolina license and that the agreement is irrevocable. The agreement does not describe the complaint, the investigation or the charges, and it contains no findings or admissions; the caption lists two investigative file numbers from 2016.
cases.outcome: Permanent relinquishment of the right to practice medicine in South Carolina, effective May 4, 2021 upon acceptance by the Board; not eligible to reapply.

narrative: The Board had filed a Notice and Formal Complaint charging the psychiatrist with violations of, among other provisions, the section of the Medical Practice Act that allows the Board to discipline a licensee upon a finding of misconduct. While denying the claims, she agreed by an Agreement to Deactivate License to permanently cease the active practice of medicine in South Carolina; her license was permanently placed in inactive status, and she agreed that she will never be eligible to reactivate it. The agreement does not describe the conduct charged in the Formal Complaint, which is not attached, and it contains no findings or admissions.
cases.outcome: License permanently placed in inactive status by agreement, effective July 1, 2021; never eligible for reactivation.

narrative: By a one-page Agreement to Deactivate License, the psychiatrist agreed that his South Carolina medical license would be permanently placed in inactive status and that he would permanently cease the active practice of medicine in the state. The agreement states only that he "has advised that he wishes" to do so. Its caption lists three Office of Investigations and Enforcement file numbers (opened in 2017, 2019 and 2021), but the document does not describe any complaint, charge, allegation or investigation, and it contains no findings or admissions. Nothing in it indicates what conduct, if any, was under review.
cases.outcome: License permanently placed in inactive status by agreement (permanent cessation of active practice in South Carolina), effective August 24, 2022.

narrative: On a showing of probable cause by the Office of Disciplinary Counsel, the Board issued an Order of Temporary Suspension finding that the public interest "imperatively requires" the immediate suspension of the psychiatrist's practice, and suspended his license effective immediately, pending a hearing and until further order. The order lists three 2022 case numbers but states no allegations or facts, so it does not say what conduct was under investigation. It was an interim action taken before any hearing; an investigator hand-delivered it two days later. The same three case numbers were later resolved by an Agreement to Deactivate License (Case 235).
cases.outcome: License temporarily suspended effective immediately, pending a hearing and until further order of the Board (interim).

narrative: This one-page Order granted the psychiatrist's petition to be released from the terms, conditions and restrictions of an Order of Reinstatement that the Board had entered on September 6, 2017. He appeared before the Board on August 5, 2024 without counsel. Based on the evidence presented, the Board found that he had complied with all of the 2017 order's terms for long enough to show that he could practice safely without them, released him from all terms, conditions and restrictions, and declared his license unrestricted and in good standing as of that date. The order does not say why the license had needed reinstatement, what the 2017 terms were, or what conduct led to the earlier action; it contains no allegations, findings or admissions about misconduct.
cases.outcome: Petition granted: released from all terms, conditions and restrictions of the 2017 Order of Reinstatement; license unrestricted and in good standing effective August 5, 2024.

narrative: The psychiatrist, licensed in South Carolina since 1980, signed an Agreement to Deactivate License under which he voluntarily ceased the active practice of medicine in the state and his license was placed in inactive status, effective immediately. Unlike a permanent deactivation, the agreement allows a return to practice, but only if he appears before the Board for reinstatement. The agreement bears the same three 2022 case numbers as the Order of Temporary Suspension issued about eight months earlier (Case 233), yet it states no allegations, findings or admissions and does not describe the matters under investigation.
cases.outcome: License placed in inactive status by agreement, effective February 26, 2025; must appear before the Board for reinstatement.
